WHY OPEN CORE?

When a resident chokes on the wrong texture, it is not an IT ticket—it is a medical emergency. Clinical dining safety, IDDSI compliance, and thermal tray tickets should be a fundamental human right in elder care, not an unaffordable luxury.

If you have ever stepped into a senior living dietary department at 4:30 PM, you know the daily high-stakes reality:

01LAST-MINUTE CLINICAL EHR CHANGES

Nursing calls down right before tray line with two room transfers, a new physician Low Sodium order, and a resident newly designated strict NPO awaiting swallow evaluation.

02GLOVED KITCHEN ERGONOMICS

Line cooks with wet nitrile gloves are trying to read faded handwriting on a greasy whiteboard while staging 4 hotel pans of hot entrees under a 165°F heat lamp.

03CLIPBOARD MRP GUESSWORK

Building weekly food orders for Dennis Food Service or Sysco using clipboards and guesswork, hoping you don't stock out of thickener or pureed meats before Friday truck delivery.

The Legacy Software Trap

When evaluating legacy healthcare dining software, independent facilities face a false binary:

Proprietary Monopolies
$1,200+/mo · Multi-Year Lock-in

Bloated software engineered in 2004 for 800-bed hospital conglomerates. Requires 6 months of IT onboarding, complex server provisioning, and exclusive distributor contracts.

Paper Binders & Spreadsheets
$0 · Maximum Survey Risk

What 80% of independent homes actually rely on. Handwritten notes, disconnected recipe sheets, and high anxiety whenever state health inspectors audit CMS F-Tag 812 compliance.

The ShorelineOps Alternative

We built ShorelineOps as a third way: an open-source, practitioner-designed operating system that runs locally on simple hardware, scales seamlessly to the cloud, and treats clinical safety with mathematical rigor.
